passages.text: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in their abundance of chariots and in their multitude of horsemen. They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Holy One of Israel.
Some people go down to Egypt for help.
They look for help from Egypt’s army.
They trust in horses.
They depend on many chariots.
They rely on a great number of horsemen.
They do not look to the Holy One of Israel.
They do not seek the LORD.
passages.original: ה֣וֹי הַיֹּרְדִ֤ים מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה עַל־ סוּסִ֖ים יִשָּׁעֵ֑נוּ וַיִּבְטְח֨וּ עַל־ רֶ֜כֶב כִּ֣י רָ֗ב וְעַ֤ל פָּֽרָשִׁים֙ כִּֽי־ עָצְמ֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד וְלֹ֤א שָׁעוּ֙ עַל־ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: Yet He too is wise and brings disaster; He does not call back His words. He will rise up against the house of the wicked and against the allies of evildoers.
passages.sermon:
God is wise.
God brings disaster.
God does not take back His words.
God rises up against the house of the wicked.
God rises up against those who help evildoers.
passages.original: וְגַם־ ה֤וּא חָכָם֙ וַיָּ֣בֵא רָ֔ע וְאֶת־ דְּבָרָ֖יו לֹ֣א הֵסִ֑יר וְקָם֙ עַל־ בֵּ֣ית מְרֵעִ֔ים וְעַל־ עֶזְרַ֖ת פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: But the Egyptians are men, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the helper will stumble, and the one he helps will fall; both will perish together.
passages.sermon:
The Egyptians are only men.
They are not God.
Their horses are made of flesh.
Their horses do not have spirit.
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD will stretch out His hand.
The one who tries to help will stumble.
The one who is helped will fall.
Both will perish together.
passages.original: וּמִצְרַ֤יִם אָדָם֙ וְֽלֹא־ אֵ֔ל וְסוּסֵיהֶ֥ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וְלֹא־ ר֑וּחַ וַֽיהוָ֞ה יַטֶּ֣ה יָד֗וֹ וְכָשַׁ֤ל עוֹזֵר֙ וְנָפַ֣ל עָזֻ֔ר וְיַחְדָּ֖ו כֻּלָּ֥ם יִכְלָיֽוּן׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD has said to me: “Like a lion roaring or a young lion over its prey— and though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor— so the LORD of Hosts will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and its heights.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD is powerful and fearless.
He said, "A lion roars over its prey.
A young lion stands over what it has caught.
Many shepherds gather against the lion.
They shout loudly at the lion.
The lion is not afraid of their voices.
The lion does not run away from their noise.
In the same way, the LORD of Hosts will come down.
The LORD will fight on Mount Zion.
The LORD will fight on its hill."
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר־ יְהוָ֣ה׀ אֵלַ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶהְגֶּה֩ הָאַרְיֵ֨ה וְהַכְּפִ֜יר עַל־ טַרְפּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקָּרֵ֤א עָלָיו֙ מְלֹ֣א רֹעִ֔ים מִקּוֹלָם֙ לֹ֣א יֵחָ֔ת וּמֵֽהֲמוֹנָ֖ם לֹ֣א יַֽעֲנֶ֑ה כֵּ֗ן יֵרֵד֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לִצְבֹּ֥א עַל־ הַר־ צִיּ֖וֹן וְעַל־ גִּבְעָתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will shield it and deliver it; He will pass over it and preserve it.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
The LORD of Hosts has great power.
The LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem.
He will protect Jerusalem like birds that hover overhead.
He will shield Jerusalem.
He will deliver Jerusalem.
He will pass over Jerusalem.
He will preserve Jerusalem.
passages.original: כְּצִפֳּרִ֣ים עָפ֔וֹת כֵּ֗ן יָגֵ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־ יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם גָּנ֥וֹן וְהִצִּ֖יל פָּסֹ֥חַ וְהִמְלִֽיט׃

passages.text: Return to the One against whom you have so blatantly rebelled, O children of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
The people of Israel have rebelled deeply against God.
God commands the people of Israel to return to Him.
God calls the children of Israel to turn back from their rebellion.
passages.original: שׁ֗וּבוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֛ר הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ סָרָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For on that day, every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He says a day will come.
On that day, each person will reject idols.
These idols are made of silver and gold.
Your own hands made these idols.
You sinned when you made them.
You will turn away from these idols.
passages.original: כִּ֚י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִמְאָס֗וּן אִ֚ישׁ אֱלִילֵ֣י כַסְפּ֔וֹ וֶאֱלִילֵ֖י זְהָב֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם יְדֵיכֶ֖ם חֵֽטְא׃

passages.text: “Then Assyria will fall, but not by the sword of man; a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals. They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor.
passages.sermon:
Assyria was a powerful nation.
Assyria will fall.
No human sword will bring down Assyria.
No weapon made by people will destroy Assyria.
A sword will devour Assyria.
This sword is not made by mortals.
Assyria will run away from the sword.
Assyria’s young men will become forced laborers.
passages.original: וְנָפַ֤ל אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּחֶ֣רֶב לֹא־ אִ֔ישׁ וְחֶ֥רֶב לֹֽא־ אָדָ֖ם תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ וְנָ֥ס לוֹ֙ מִפְּנֵי־ חֶ֔רֶב וּבַחוּרָ֖יו לָמַ֥ס יִהְיֽוּ׃

passages.text: Their rock will pass away for fear, and their princes will panic at the sight of the battle standard,” declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD has fire in Zion.
The LORD has a furnace in Jerusalem.
Their rock will disappear because of fear.
Their princes will panic and run away.
passages.original: וְסַלְעוֹ֙ מִמָּג֣וֹר יַֽעֲב֔וֹר וְחַתּ֥וּ מִנֵּ֖ס שָׂרָ֑יו נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־ א֥וּר לוֹ֙ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וְתַנּ֥וּר ל֖וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס
